== Biography ==

Cotton-tail is one of four young rabbits who live together in a sand-bank beneath the root of a very big fir-tree. She has two sisters, Flopsy and Mopsy, and a brother, Peter. Like her sisters, Cotton-tail is a good little bunny.

On the day when their mother went out to the baker's shop, Cotton-tail went with Flopsy and Mopsy down the lane to gather blackberries. The three good little bunnies attended to their task together.

Her brother Peter, however, was of quite a different sort. Being rather naughty, he ran straight away to Mr. McGregor's garden, squeezed under the gate, and ate lettuces, French beans, and radishes until he felt rather sick.

When evening came, Peter lay in bed being given camomile tea as a remedy, while Cotton-tail sat down to supper with Flopsy and Mopsy, enjoying bread, milk, and the blackberries they had gathered.

== Narrative role ==

Cotton-tail is one of four little Rabbits born into a family that dwells in a sand-bank beneath the root of a very big fir-tree. She lives there with her Mother and her three siblings: Flopsy, [[Mopsy]], and Peter. Among the four, Cotton-tail is known as a good little bunny—a virtue that characterizes her from the beginning.

One day, Cotton-tail sets out with her good siblings Flopsy and Mopsy down the lane to gather blackberries. The three travel together on this wholesome expedition, gathering their fruit in a manner befitting good little bunnies. Their brother Peter does not accompany them on this virtuous errand; instead, he runs naughtily to Mr. McGregor's garden.

The contrast between Cotton-tail's path and Peter's is stark. While Cotton-tail and her siblings Flopsy and Mopsy labor at their honest gathering, Peter pursues recklessness and mischief. Cotton-tail remains steadfast in her virtue.

Thus Cotton-tail's character emerges: a good little bunny rooted in her family home, participating in its wholesome life, and standing in quiet contrast to her brother's waywardness.

== Personality ==

Cotton-tail is obedient and conscientious. Described as one of the 'good little bunnies,' Cotton-tail demonstrates respect for maternal authority and willingness to follow instruction. This disposition stands in marked contrast to Peter's recklessness—where Peter ventured into the forbidden garden and met with sickness, Cotton-tail attended dutifully to gathering blackberries as directed.

This reliable conduct reveals a steadiness of temperament that suggests sound judgment. Cotton-tail's acceptance of maternal guidance, while Peter pursued transgression, illustrates a character inclined toward propriety and familial duty rather than impulsive independence. The comfort of Cotton-tail's ordinary supper—bread, milk, and blackberries gathered through proper conduct—stands as quiet testament to the advantages of obedience.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Flopsy]]''' — sister and companion in good behaviour. Flopsy shares Cotton-tail's obedient nature; both are counted among the good little bunnies and went together down the lane to gather blackberries, as their Mother bade them do.

'''[[Mopsy]]''' — sister and companion in good behaviour. Like Cotton-tail and Flopsy, Mopsy is a good little bunny and ventured with them to gather blackberries, staying within the bounds of propriety that their wayward brother Peter did not.

'''[[Peter]]''' — brother, though of very different temperament. Where Cotton-tail proved obedient and virtuous, Peter was very naughty indeed. He ran straight away to Mr. McGregor's garden despite their Mother's warning, ate lettuces, beans, and radishes until he felt rather sick, and was punished with a dose of camomile tea at bedtime; Cotton-tail meanwhile enjoyed a good supper of bread and milk and blackberries.

'''[[Rabbit]]''' — mother, provider and guardian. Cotton-tail and siblings make their home with their Mother in a sand-bank beneath the root of a very big fir-tree. She gives them guidance, warning them of dangers, and provides them with bread, milk, and other sustenance.
